Yangtze Floods Disrupt Power Supply and Industry Across China

Heavy flooding along the Yangtze River has caused widespread disruption to economic activity across central and eastern China, with power generation and manufacturing sectors among the hardest hit. Authorities report that torrential rains, which began four days ago, have pushed river levels to their highest since 1998, inundating cities and agricultural land across Hubei, Anhui, and Jiangsu provinces.

SDIC Power Holdings Co Ltd confirmed on Wednesday that several of its hydropower stations along the river have been forced to halt operations as a precautionary measure. “Ensuring the safety of our facilities and the communities nearby is our top priority,” said Wang Lei, a spokesperson for the company. “We are working closely with local authorities to monitor water levels and resume normal operations as soon as conditions allow.”

The China Federation of Industrial Enterprises estimates that over 200 factories in the flood zone have temporarily suspended activities due to power shortages and flooded transport links. “The ongoing situation is putting significant strain on supply chains across a range of sectors, from electronics to textiles,” said analyst Lin Hua. “It’s a critical period for recovery, as many businesses were already facing challenges from previous disruptions.”

Local officials have warned that further rainfall is expected over the coming days, and emergency crews remain on standby. The Ministry of Water Resources has raised the flood alert and is coordinating with affected provinces to reinforce embankments and evacuate residents where necessary. As the situation continues to unfold, authorities urge the public to stay alert to official updates.
